identity: The Gospel of Luke 12:54 – 13:35 in the Van Dyck Arabic version. Seven <NL>-delimited pericopes: reading the signs of the times (12:54-59), the Galileans and the tower of Siloam (13:1-5), the barren fig tree (13:6-9), the crippled woman healed on the Sabbath (13:10-17), the mustard seed (13:18-19), the leaven (13:20-21), the narrow door (13:22-30), and the lament over Jerusalem (13:31-35). Van Dyck vocabulary and orthography throughout — هوذا، كلا، ههنا، البتة، الكرّام، مذود، صرير الأسنان — with two run-together scan artifacts, 'ياأورشليم' @562 and 'مباركالآتي' @599.
law: §M, and §M1 is the whole of it: A ‖ IN SCRIPTURE MARKS A VERSE NUMBER, NOT A SENTENCE. The verse numbers were stripped, the annotators segmented on them, and internal full stops inside a verse are IGNORED. I identified the 41 verses of Luke 12:54-13:35 and placed a boundary on the last token of each. 602 tokens / 41 verses = 14.7 tokens per verse — the short end of §M's 15-35 band, which is right for Luke.
reasoning:
Every trap §M2 names is present in this passage and I refused all of them.
- Speech verbs never separate from their quotation: فأجاب يسوع وقال لهم (13:2), فقال للكرّام (13:7), وقال لها يا امرأة (13:12), فأجابه الرب وقال يا مرائي (13:15), وقال أيضا (13:20), فقال لهم امضوا (13:32). The boundary always lands on the last token BEFORE the verb.
- Questions never separate: أتظنون … لأنهم كابدوا مثل هذا (13:2), لماذا تبطل الأرض أيضا (13:7), ألا يحل كل واحد منكم … ويسقيه (13:15), أما كان ينبغي أن تحل … في يوم السبت (13:16), أقليل هم الذين يخلصون (13:23). T8 as refined: a question welds inside a verse.
- ف / ثم / و never separate inside a verse: 13:13 'ووضع عليها يديه ففي الحال استقامت ومجدت الله' is ONE verse with three clauses; 13:19 'أخذها إنسان وألقاها في بستانه فنمت وصارت شجرة كبيرة وتآوت طيور السماء في أغصانها' is one verse with four; 13:29's fourfold ومن … ومن … والجنوب ويتكئون is one verse.
- Internal full stops are ignored, which is where the length comes from: 13:25 runs 28 tokens across three printed sentences ('… افتح لنا. يجيب ويقول لكم: لا أعرفكم من أين أنتم.') and 13:7 across three ('… ولم أجد. اقطعها! لماذا تبطل الأرض أيضا؟'). Under a punctuation reading I would have cut both; under §M1 they are single verses.
- Vocatives weld here, unlike in dialogue (H3): 'يا مرائي' opens 13:15 and 'يا أورشليم ياأورشليم يا قاتلة الأنبياء' opens 13:34, both inside their verse.
The one break that looks wrong and is right: @404 لهم. Luke 13:23 ends with the bare speech-verb phrase 'فقال لهم' and the quotation 'اجتهدوا أن تدخلوا من الباب الضيق' opens 13:24. §M2 records exactly this — 'a speech verb can end a verse with the quote starting the next' (doc_4f0612ce35d1 @295, which I MISSED in batch 2). Medium, since a handful of editions attach فقال لهم forward.
Similarly @221: 13:10 is the seven-token fragment 'وكان يعلم في أحد المجامع في السبت' and the وإذا امرأة clause is 13:11. Short verses are normal in §M and I did not merge them.
The seven <NL> boundaries (@81, @157, @213, @340, @365, @384, @507) all coincide with verse ends, as they must, and the final token @601 closes 13:35.
